headline: High-risk default write/network agent paired with PDF browser worker creates medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure; compliance risk is low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenHands can read/write mounted files, run browsers, and use MCP; pdf.js processes PDF files in a browser-based worker. If OpenHands ingests pdf.js outputs or PDFs as trusted instructions, malicious document content can steer actions. The shared file bridge is plausible, but the pair lacks explicit provenance tracking.
conditions: IF OpenHands reads pdf.js-produced text or PDFs as instructions without provenance checks
IF both agents share the same mounted volume or file handoff path
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following from PDF text
Add a provenance tag to every file handoff
Keep pdf.js outputs in a read-only staging folder
Require manual review before OpenHands acts on document content

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenHands touches files mounted into its runtime and handles model-provider API keys; pdf.js opens PDF files. If sensitive PDFs are placed in the shared runtime volume, both agents can access them, and OpenHands may transmit context to its configured model provider. The pair therefore has a realistic shared-workspace leakage path.
conditions: IF sensitive PDFs are mounted into the same runtime volume used by OpenHands
IF OpenHands sends document contents to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Separate sensitive PDFs from OpenHands workspaces
Use a local-only model provider for OpenHands
Redact secrets before handing files to either agent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress; pdf.js is read-oriented but can still operate on the same PDF files. The main conflict is not direct write-write contention, but OpenHands can mutate shared files while pdf.js reads them, causing inconsistent state in default shared-volume setups.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same mounted directory
IF OpenHands modifies files while pdf.js is reading them
mitigations: Make PDF inputs immutable during processing
Serialize access with a simple lock file
Avoid letting OpenHands edit files that pdf.js is consuming

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands can generate edits or analysis from browser and shell actions, and pdf.js can render or process PDFs. If pdf.js output is treated as authoritative by OpenHands, errors or hallucinated interpretations can cascade into downstream file edits or commits. The pair lacks a built-in verification step in the profiles, so uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF OpenHands uses pdf.js output as source material for edits or commits
IF no human or automated verification step checks extracted text before action
mitigations: Block direct commits from document-derived content
Ask for human approval before any downstream action

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch. OpenHands handles model-provider API keys and runtime files, while pdf.js handles PDFs, but no PHI/EU-only flow or retention conflict is documented. The other agent is not cited beyond confirming its PDF-only scope.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into the shared runtime
IF the configured model provider or storage policy imposes stricter retention than the PDF workflow
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Document retention settings for both tools
Use a local deployment for sensitive documents
